test_title: PYST 54: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

She has taken / nothing from yesterday / and is feeling / nauseatic now.
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. nauseatic now .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **“nauseatic”** is incorrect because it is not a valid word in English. The correct term to describe feeling sick is **“nauseous”**.
 
• The sentence should read: **“She has taken nothing from yesterday and is feeling nauseous now.”**
 
• All other segments of the sentence are grammatically correct and do not contain any spelling errors.

Correct sentence: *She has taken nothing from yesterday and is feeling **nauseous** now*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nauseous:** A proper adjective used to describe the feeling of sickness or queasiness, often associated with an urge to vomit.
 
• **Common Mistake:** Words like “nauseatic” are sometimes used mistakenly, but they are not recognized in standard English.
 
• **Usage Tip:** To describe the state of feeling sick, always use “nauseous” or “nauseated.”
